question: What happens to my policy when I die?
answer: When you pass away, your named beneficiary contacts the insurance carrier to file a claim. The carrier pays the death benefit — the full face amount of your policy — directly to your beneficiary. The payment is typically made within 7 to 30 days of receiving a completed claim package. The money goes directly to your beneficiary and does not go through probate.

question: How does my beneficiary get the money?
answer: Your beneficiary contacts the insurance company after you pass away, submits a completed claim form along with a certified copy of the death certificate, and the carrier processes the payment — typically within 7 to 30 days. The death benefit is paid directly to your beneficiary, usually as a lump sum, and is generally tax-free. Julie can help your family through this process if needed.

question: Is there a death waiting period?
answer: Some final expense policies have a waiting period — usually 2 years — during which the full death benefit is not payable if the insured dies from a non-accidental cause. During this period, the beneficiary typically receives a return of premiums paid plus interest. After the waiting period, the full death benefit applies. Not all policies have waiting periods — many applicants qualify for immediate (level) coverage with no waiting period based on their health answers.

question: Can I borrow against my policy?
answer: Some whole life insurance policies accumulate cash value over time, which you may be able to borrow against. However, for most final expense policies, the primary purpose is the death benefit — cash value growth is modest and borrowing against it is not a primary feature. If you're interested in a policy with meaningful cash value access, mention this to Julie so she can find the right fit.

question: ¿Qué es un período de espera?
answer: Un período de espera en un seguro de vida es un tiempo específico — generalmente 2 años — durante el cual el beneficio completo por fallecimiento no está disponible si el asegurado muere por causas no accidentales. Durante ese período, el beneficiario generalmente recibe un reembolso de las primas pagadas más intereses. Después del período de espera, el beneficio completo aplica. No todas las pólizas tienen período de espera — muchos solicitantes califican para cobertura inmediata (nivel) según sus respuestas de salud.
